name: props_street_guardrail
prompt:
One image is attached: finished art from the same game — the grass these things stand on and two cars, at one scale — to match in style, finish and scale only, not its contents or colours.

Make one image of 12 separate sprites for a 2D city game seen from above: roadside furniture along an intercity highway outside town — steel crash barriers and their ends, a concrete median, a crash cushion, a drum and a marker post. Lay them in a 4 by 3 grid — 3 rows of 4, read left to right and top to bottom in the order listed below — each centred in its place in the grid, well apart from its neighbours and from the picture's edge, never touching another.

Size and shape:
- Each is drawn at the true size given, in metres, against the cars in the style image (4.5 m long, 1.8 m wide): a smaller thing is drawn smaller than a larger one, in proportion. A round thing is as wide as it is deep; a rectangular one keeps the proportion given.
- Every made object has clean straight or round edges. Nothing is cut off.
- A barrier section lies horizontally, its length along the picture's width. The game lays sections end to end along a road, so a section's end marked "cut straight and square" is a crisp vertical edge with the beam (or the concrete) reaching right to it at full width: no end cap, no taper, no gap, no post at the very end. Its two ends are the same height and in line, so the next section continues it seamlessly.
- Seen straight down, a steel beam shows its narrow top edge and the posts behind it show their small square tops; a concrete barrier shows its top ridge and its sloped faces from above. No face of a barrier seen from the side.

Scale of the details is strict: a post top about 15 cm square, a spacer block about as large, a beam about 10 cm wide seen from above. A small thing keeps its details few, simple and readable.

The view:
- A thing marked "front at the bottom" is turned in the game to face the traffic, so it is seen strictly from directly above (orthographic plan view, like a map), its front at the bottom edge: no perspective, no tilt, no side faces.
- Everything else is never turned, so it may be seen from high above at a slight angle, a little of its side showing towards the bottom, as long as it reads mostly from above: a tree is mostly its crown, a bin mostly its lid.
- No cast shadow on the ground; soft shading on the thing itself, light from the top-left.

Style: painted game art like the style image, natural and believable rather than cartoonish: soft detailed painting, no heavy black outlines, rich but natural colours, every drawing clearly different from its neighbours. Summer, in a Black Sea port city.

Everything outside the drawings is fully transparent: no background colour, no ground, no grass under them, no shadow, nothing half-transparent. No text, letters, numbers, logos, labels, grid lines or frames anywhere.

Drawings, row by row, left to right:


Row 1
1. 4 x 0.45 m (8.9x wider than deep, front at the bottom) — new galvanised steel W-beam crash barrier section, 4 m long: a narrow bright silver-grey steel beam runs the whole length along the bottom edge, its corrugated profile showing as two thin parallel ridges along it; just behind it two small square steel posts, each with a short spacer block joining it to the beam, one a quarter of the way in from each end; both ends cut straight and square, the beam reaching right to them, so sections join end to end
2. 4 x 0.45 m (8.9x wider than deep, front at the bottom) — the same 4 m W-beam crash barrier section weathered: dull grey galvanising with soft brown rust spots and road grime, two posts a quarter of the way in from each end, both ends cut straight and square
3. 4 x 0.6 m (6.7x wider than deep, front at the bottom) — double-sided W-beam median barrier section, 4 m long: two galvanised steel beams run the whole length along both long edges, two square steel posts between them a quarter of the way in from each end, both ends cut straight and square
4. 4 x 0.6 m (6.7x wider than deep, front at the bottom) — precast concrete highway median barrier section, 4 m long: light grey concrete, a narrow flat top ridge along its middle, the sloped faces either side of it shaded, both ends cut straight and square

Row 2
5. 2 x 0.45 m (4.4x wider than deep, front at the bottom) — the same new galvanised W-beam section, 2 m long: the beam runs the whole length along the bottom edge, one square steel post with its spacer block at the middle behind it, both ends cut straight and square
6. 2 x 0.45 m (4.4x wider than deep, front at the bottom) — the same 2 m W-beam section weathered: dull grey with soft brown rust spots, one post at the middle, both ends cut straight and square
7. 2 x 0.9 m (2.2x wider than deep, front at the bottom) — flared terminal end of a W-beam crash barrier, 2 m long: at the left end the galvanised beam lies along the bottom edge, cut straight and square to join a run; towards the right it curves smoothly away up to the top edge and ends in a rounded steel fishtail end cap; one post behind it at the middle
8. 1 x 0.45 m (2.2x wider than deep, front at the bottom) — short end of a W-beam crash barrier, 1 m long: the galvanised beam along the bottom edge, the left end cut straight and square to join a run, the right end a rounded steel fishtail cap bent back, one post at the middle

Row 3
9. 4 x 0.5 m (8.0x wider than deep, front at the bottom) — the same new 4 m W-beam section dented by a crash: the beam pushed back towards the posts in its middle in a shallow bend, scuffed bare steel and a smear of black tyre rubber there, two posts a quarter of the way in from each end, both ends straight and square and in line
10. 2.5 x 0.9 m (2.8x wider than deep, rounded corners, front at the bottom) — highway crash cushion at a barrier's end: a row of yellow plastic energy-absorbing segments on a dark steel frame, its rounded nose at the right with black and yellow diagonal chevron stripes
11. round, 0.6 m across — orange and white plastic road channelizing drum seen from above: a round orange top with a white ring, a black rubber base ring showing round it
12. 0.15 x 0.12 m (1.2x wider than deep, front at the bottom) — white plastic roadside delineator post seen from above: a small white post top with a black band across it and an orange reflector on its front
